papers.title: Exact 1D Nonlinear Solutions for Proton-Driven Plasma Wakefields
papers.abstract: We extend the classical 1D nonlinear relativistic plasma wakefield paradigm to evaluate the pristine fluid profiles driven by intense relativistic proton trains under the comoving coordinate approximation. Using an intense two-bunch scheme, our adaptive integration model is validated down to machine precision against exact closed-form cold-fluid invariants, confirming that interface boundary corners represent physical step discontinuities in the second potential derivative. Scaling to an $N=100$ micro-bunch train, we resolve macroscopic phase-accumulation and subsequent nonlinear detuning by deriving a closed-form, parameter-free piecewise analytical envelope expression. This solution successfully maps the initial unattenuated quadratic coherent growth alongside the flat asymptotic horizontal saturation horizon governed by nonlinear energy conservation. Furthermore, the framework analytically evaluates the transient envelope overshoot, tracking its decay onto the saturation boundary via an exact phase-slip integration length scale. Providing immediate, ready macro-envelope bounds, this computationally inexpensive tool eliminates empirical adjustments and yields a robust mathematical baseline designed to guide and accelerate complex, multi-dimensional particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations through rapid parameter space exploration before deploying heavy computational assets. It establishes an efficient foundation to optimize asymmetric, custom-shaped driver profiles required to break the fundamental symmetric transformer ratio limit of 2 to make current particle accelerators more efficient.

papers.title: Physics-constrained graph closures and working-point conditioning for a fast surrogate of linac beam dynamics
papers.abstract: When a graph neural network estimates a physical quantity, its frame, edge direction, aggregation and feature normalization decide which laws it can break. Wrong choices leave systematic errors the loss never registers. We build a linac beam-dynamics surrogate on this observation. Space charge, short-range wakefields and coherent synchrotron radiation enter as bounded closures on analytic kernels, on graphs whose frame and direction follow the interaction and whose symmetry makes the net space-charge self-force vanish for any weights. Verified without training, with randomized weights, the invariants break by five to eight orders of magnitude once the responsible feature is inverted. Per-working-point models constrained by the rms envelope equation are distilled into one model conditioned on 15 machine settings. On the 18.4~m L0+L1 section of the Shanghai soft x-ray free-electron laser linac, this model predicts the transverse beam envelope at 50 unseen settings to about $7\%$, with the centroid trajectory and emittance, in 0.38~s on a single Quadro RTX 6000 GPU. Training is instead dominated by a normalization choice, a data-derived output range for the beam size: at all 16 working points it lowers the starting error 2.2- to 8.5-fold and fixes the convergence speed. The remaining accuracy differences between hybrid and data-driven architectures vary with the working point and with the density of observation. The held-out error scales roughly as $N^{-0.6}$ with the corpus size $N$. Whether the physics pays off where collective effects are strong, as in a magnetic bunch compressor, is in the next phase of our study.
